name: XOS Console
tagline: Platform operations for the XOS team.

auth.title: Sign in to the operator console
auth.intro: The console is for the XOS platform team. Sign in with your platform account; every action needs your second factor.

errors.invalid_credentials: That email and password do not match an account.
errors.not_operator: This console is for the XOS platform team, and your account is not on it, so you were signed out.
errors.provider_disabled: That way of signing in is not turned on here.
errors.provider_error: Sign in with Google did not finish. Try again.
errors.link_invalid: That sign-in expired or started in another browser. Sign in again.
errors.over_request_rate_limit: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.unexpected: Sign-in did not work. Try again.

secondFactor.title: Confirm it is you
secondFactor.intro: Every console action needs a second factor. Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
secondFactor.enrollIntro: Every console action needs a second factor. Add an authenticator app to your account to continue.
secondFactor.label: Name
secondFactor.qr: QR code that sets up {name} in an authenticator app
secondFactor.keyHelp: Can't scan? Type this setup key into your authenticator app.
secondFactor.keysOnly: Your account has only security keys. The console takes an authenticator app for now: set one up below.

errors.code_invalid: That code did not match. Enter the current code from your app.
errors.code_expired: That code expired. Enter the current one.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.unexpected: The code could not be checked. Try again.

common.reasonHelp: Kept in the console ledger and, for a tenant, in its audit log.
common.loadError: This could not be loaded. Reload the page to try again.

errors.invalid: Check the fields and try again.
errors.notFound: That was not found, or your role cannot do it.
errors.conflict: Something changed while you worked. Reload and try again.
errors.unexpected: That did not work. Try again.
errors.step_up_required: Confirm it is you with your second factor, then try again.

refusals.console_unknown_plan: Choose a plan from the list.
refusals.plan_override_reason: Say why, in up to 500 characters.
refusals.plan_override_expiry: An override ends within a year.
refusals.plan_override_shape: Choose a plan, a feature and whether it is on, or a limit and its value.
refusals.flag_unknown: Choose a flag from the list.
refusals.flag_override_reason: Say why, in up to 300 characters.
refusals.flag_override_expiry: An override ends within a year.
refusals.flag_kill_switch_reason: Say why, in up to 500 characters.
refusals.support_session_closed: This support session has ended. The Owner can grant a new one.
refusals.support_session_ended: This support session has already ended.
refusals.moderation_ground: Removing or restricting needs a ground of illegal content or a breach of the terms. No action and restoring mean no violation.
refusals.moderation_not_removed: Only a removed or restricted listing can be restored.
refusals.moderation_rule_reference: Name the law or the terms clause relied on, in up to 300 characters.
refusals.moderation_facts: State the facts the decision rests on, in up to 4,000 characters.
refusals.moderation_statement: Write the statement of reasons, in up to 4,000 characters.
refusals.moderation_report_mismatch: The report must be one on this listing.
refusals.moderation_appeal_decided: This appeal has already been decided.
refusals.moderation_appeal_outcome: Uphold the decision or reverse it.
refusals.moderation_appeal_new_decision: Reversing a decision to take no action needs the new decision: remove or restrict, with its ground, rule and facts.
refusals.system_banner_shape: Choose the kind, the severity and who sees the banner.
refusals.system_banner_message: Write the banner in up to 300 characters.
refusals.system_banner_incident_link: An incident banner links to the status page.
refusals.system_banner_maintenance_window: A maintenance banner needs the end of its window.
refusals.system_banner_window: The banner must end after it starts, in the future and within 90 days.
refusals.system_banner_critical_dismissible: A Critical banner cannot be dismissed.
refusals.system_banner_ended: An ended banner never changes. Publish a new one.
refusals.operator_reason: Say why, in up to 500 characters.
refusals.operator_no_account: No account uses that email. The person signs up once, then gets the role.
refusals.operator_self: You never grant yourself a role.
refusals.operator_exists: This person is already on the platform team. Revoke the role first to change it.
refusals.operator_last_administrator: The platform team keeps at least one Administrator. Grant another first.
refusals.funnel_alert_missing: That funnel alert no longer exists. Reload the page.
refusals.funnel_alert_resolved: The funnel recovered and its alert is closed.
refusals.legal_queue_title: Describe it in up to 200 characters.
refusals.legal_queue_received: Say when it arrived. That cannot be in the future.
refusals.legal_queue_due: Enter the date the document sets, after the day it arrived.
refusals.legal_queue_subject: No account uses that email. Leave it empty if the content has no account behind it.
refusals.legal_queue_related: Name the reference of the DMCA notice this answers.
refusals.legal_queue_org: Name the organization by its slug, as the Tenants page shows it. If its data is already deleted, add the request as another written promise and tell the person nothing is left to return.
refusals.legal_hold_queue: This hold belongs to an open return of omitted data. Close that item to release it.
refusals.org_read_only: This organization is read-only, so the change was not saved.
refusals.legal_queue_note: Say what was done, in up to 4,000 characters.
refusals.legal_queue_first_response: This item has no first response waiting.
refusals.legal_queue_fed: This item follows its source. Act on the source, and it follows.
refusals.transition_reason_required: Every state change carries a reason.
refusals.legal_queue_item_transition_not_allowed: An item cannot move to that state from where it is.
refusals.legal_queue_item_state_conflict: The item has moved since this page loaded. Reload it.
refusals.legal_queue_court_action: A court action applies only when completing a DMCA counter-notice.
refusals.legal_queue_too_early: The statute does not allow this before its earliest day. Wait for it, or record the court action.
refusals.legal_queue_extended: This item can no longer be extended.
refusals.legal_queue_extension_late: An extension must be taken, and the person told, before the first period ends.
refusals.legal_queue_extension_reason: Say why, in up to 1,000 characters, as you will tell the person.
refusals.legal_contact_name: Say who this is, in up to 200 characters.
refusals.legal_contact_exists: This address already gets overdue alerts.
refusals.legal_contact_missing: That contact was already removed. Reload the page.
refusals.outside_reviewer_name: Name the reviewer, in up to 200 characters.
refusals.outside_reviewer_organization: Keep the firm or body to 200 characters.
refusals.outside_reviewer_reason: Say why, in up to 500 characters.
refusals.outside_reviewer_exists: An outside reviewer is already appointed. End that appointment first.
refusals.outside_reviewer_missing: That appointment has already ended. Reload the page.
refusals.moderation_appeal_re_review: Record what you looked at again and how you weighed the grounds, in up to 4,000 characters.
refusals.moderation_appeal_outside_reviewer: This appeal goes to the outside reviewer. Record their decision once they have made it.
refusals.legal_queue_re_review: Record what you looked at again and how you weighed the grounds, in up to 4,000 characters.
refusals.legal_queue_person_told: Say how and when you told the person the result and the reasons, in up to 1,000 characters.
refusals.territory_reason: Say why, in up to 500 characters.
refusals.territory_code: Use 2 to 8 capital letters or digits, starting with a letter.
refusals.territory_name: Give the name in English and Spanish, in up to 100 characters each.
refusals.territory_country_taken: A country belongs to one territory. Take it out of the other one first.
refusals.territory_currency_unpriced: Choose currencies the price book has.
refusals.territory_code_taken: A territory already has that code. Edit it from the list.
refusals.territory_unknown: Choose a territory from the list.
refusals.territory_transition_not_allowed: The territory is already in that state. Refresh the page.
refusals.territory_last_offered: XOS must stay offered somewhere. Open another territory first.
refusals.territory_exception_email: Enter the email of the organization's first Owner.
refusals.territory_exception_not_needed: XOS is already offered in that country, so no exception is needed.
refusals.territory_exception_contract: Name the signed contract, in up to 200 characters.
refusals.territory_exception_signed_on: An exception needs a contract that is already signed: enter its date.
refusals.territory_exception_open: An open exception already names this person and country.
refusals.territory_exception_unknown: Choose an exception from the list.
refusals.territory_exception_transition_not_allow: Only an open exception can be withdrawn. Refresh the page.
refusals.rating_dispute_own: Another operator decides this dispute: it is your own.
refusals.sod_rating_dispute_decide: Another operator decides this dispute: you belong to the organization that gave the rating.
refusals.rating_dispute_outcome: Uphold the dispute or do not.
refusals.rating_dispute_decision_ground: Upholding needs a named ground: the wrong person, a false statement, abuse or personal data. A low score or an unfavorable opinion is not one.
refusals.rating_dispute_statement: Write the reasons the person and the organization receive, in up to 4,000 characters.
refusals.rating_dispute_transition_not_allowed: This dispute has already been decided.
refusals.billing_alert_reason: Say what was done about it, in up to 500 characters.

tenants.title: Tenants
tenants.intro: Find an org by name, slug, Owner email or plan. You see billing and identity facts only; records open only through a support session the Owner grants.
tenants.none: No org matches. Try part of the name, the slug or the Owner's email.

tenant.extraSeats: {count, plural, one {# extra seat} other {# extra seats}}
tenant.clients: {count, plural, one {# client org} other {# client orgs}}
tenant.readOnlyUntil: Canceled; read-only until {until}, data deleted after {purge}.
tenant.planOverridesIntro: An override changes the plan, one feature or one limit until it ends. Billing keeps the subscription's plan.
tenant.newFeatureOverride: Turn a feature on or off
tenant.partnerClientsOff: This org cannot create client orgs. Turn it on only under a signed partner agreement.
tenant.partnerClientsOn: This org may create client orgs, turned on {when}: {reason}
tenant.partnerClientsUnknown: Whether this org may create client orgs could not be read.
tenant.noActivity: No console action on this org yet.

flags.title: Feature flags
flags.intro: Defaults, plan requirements and per-org overrides. The kill switch turns a feature off everywhere at once.

territories.title: Territories
territories.intro: Where XOS is offered. A closed territory's prices and languages stay switched off, and no organization can start there. Opening one changes signup at once, and prices and languages usually within a minute and at most about 11 minutes. Before you open a territory, confirm what its law requires, such as appointed representatives and localized terms, and say so in the reason.
territories.editIntro: This form starts from what the territory holds now. Saving replaces its countries, currencies and languages, so whatever you take out leaves the territory.
territories.editOpen: This territory is open, so a change reaches signup at once.
territories.codeHelp: A two-letter country code, or a short name such as EEA. A new territory starts closed.
territories.codeFixed: The code stays as it is.
territories.nameHelp: As it reads in "offered to organizations in the United States".
territories.currenciesHelp: The first one is what its organizations pay in. None means US dollars.
territories.exceptionsIntro: An exception lets one organization start outside the offered territories, for a contract already signed, including a United States customer's contract with a vendor company. It names the first Owner's email and the country, and it is used once; a company account and its later start in Atlas each need one. It does not open the territory, and it appoints no representative: confirm what that country's law requires first.
territories.ownerEmailHelp: The organization can only be started by the person signed in with this email, once they have confirmed it.
territories.contractHelp: Its number, or where it is filed.
territories.exceptionUsedGone: Used; the organization was later deleted
territories.outsideIntro: Organizations using Atlas and Gateway company accounts whose stated country is outside the offered territories, or who stated none. Nothing happens to them automatically: review them yourself.

support.title: Support sessions
support.intro: Open platform support sessions an org's Owner granted. While one lasts you may read the org's overview, members, projects and settings; every read is logged for the org.
support.none: No platform support session is open. An org's Owner grants one in Atlas, under Settings, Security.
support.sessionIntro: Granted for: {reason}. Ends {ends}. The org sees each area you open.
support.closed: This support session has ended. The Owner can grant a new one.

moderation.title: Moderation
moderation.intro: Reported listings and appeals. Each decision carries a statement of reasons the affected party receives, and each appeal gets a fresh, documented re-review.
moderation.ruleReferenceHelp: For example: Acceptable Use Policy, Section 3, or the law and article.
moderation.statementHelp: Sent to the affected party as written. Say what you decided, why and that they may appeal within six months.
moderation.automatedNone: None: a person detected and decided this.
moderation.appealOwn: You made the decision this appeal is about. Look at it afresh: the record and the notice to the person will both say the same person re-reviewed it.
moderation.newDecision: New decision, when reversing no action
moderation.appealOutside: This appeal goes to {name}, the outside reviewer. Record their decision once they have made it.
moderation.reReviewHelp: Kept on the record and never sent. Say what you re-read and how you weighed the grounds.
moderation.reviewerSame: The person who made the first decision re-reviewed it.
moderation.notTold: This person has no email left, so they have not been told. It is in the Legal Queue with its own clock.
moderation.toldByOperator: The person was told another way on {when}. The legal queue log says how.
moderation.noticeOnItsWay: The email telling the person the result is on its way.
moderation.noticeGone: The person has not been told. The email never left, and it has since been deleted, with their account or when its Legal Queue item closed.
moderation.noticeFailed: The email telling the person the result failed, so they have not been told. It is in the Legal Queue with its own clock.

grounds.Terms Violation: Breach of the terms and policies

banners.title: System banners
banners.intro: Maintenance windows, incidents, plan notices and other notices at the top of Atlas, Gateway and Compass. Shells pick up a change within a minute.
banners.messageEsHelp: Optional. Spanish speakers see the English text without it.
banners.linkHelp: An https link, such as the status page. Required for an incident.
banners.startsHelp: Your local time. Empty starts now.
banners.endsHelp: Your local time, within 90 days. Required for maintenance; an incident may run until you end it.

funnels.title: Workflow Funnels
funnels.intro: The funnel of each workflow in Sections 11.11 to 11.13 over the last 24 hours, from consented product analytics: sessions that started, reached each step and completed, against the workflow's target and its previous 7 days. Counts only, never a person, an org or a page address.
funnels.checkedAt: Figures as of {when}. The hourly check runs at 23 minutes past each hour.
funnels.alertsIntro: The hourly check raises an alert for the owning team when a funnel falls below its target, or more than a quarter below its previous 7 days, with at least 20 started sessions. It closes the alert once the funnel recovers.
funnels.funnelsIntro: Stages read started, then each step, then completed. Rates are completed over started sessions.
funnels.alertFigures: Completed {rate} of {started} started sessions; target {target}, previous 7 days {baseline}.

team.title: Platform team
team.intro: Who may use the console and with which role. Support handles tenants, flags, banners and support sessions; Trust and Safety handles moderation; Administrators do everything, including plans and this list.
team.emailHelp: The person signs up for an XOS account first.

activity.title: Activity
activity.intro: Every console action, newest first: who did what, to which org and why.

metrics.title: Platform Metrics
metrics.intro: Platform-wide figures read from the XOS database: totals only, never a tenant's records. Weeks start on Monday and months on the 1st, in UTC.

growth.title: Growth
growth.intro: New orgs and sign-ups by week.
growth.clients: {count, plural, one {# partner client} other {# partner clients}}
growth.chart: New orgs and sign-ups by week

active.title: Active people
active.intro: People who signed in or used a signed-in session.

plans.title: Plans and trials
plans.intro: Orgs by the plan and state of their live subscription. Plan overrides are left out; billing keeps the subscription's plan.
plans.chart: Orgs by plan and subscription state

usage.title: Usage
usage.intro: Closed monthly usage totals across every org, for the last three months.
usage.none: No month has closed with usage yet.

aurora.title: Aurora
aurora.intro: Aurora requests by week, and their outcomes, features and tokens over the last 30 days.
aurora.inputTokens: Input tokens in the last 30 days
aurora.outputTokens: Output tokens in the last 30 days

jobs.title: Job queue
jobs.intro: Background jobs by kind: waiting now, and finished in the last 24 hours. A job running for more than 30 minutes is stalled.
jobs.none: No job is waiting, running or finished in the last 24 hours.

notifications.title: Notification delivery
notifications.intro: Email, text message and push deliveries of notifications from the last 7 days, by channel. The failure rate counts failed and bounced deliveries among those settled.

actionNames.legal_queue_noted: Added to a legal queue log

notFound.title: Not found
notFound.body: This page does not exist, or your role cannot open it.

error.title: This page did not load
error.body: Something went wrong while loading it. Try again; if it keeps failing, reload the page.

legalQueue.title: Legal Queue
legalQueue.intro: Every legal and security clock in one list, by the clock that comes next. Each due date comes from its clock's rule. Alerts go out before a clock ends and every day it is overdue.
legalQueue.none: Nothing is waiting. Add anything that arrives by mailbox, letter or call.
legalQueue.loadError: The queue could not load. Your mailboxes still hold everything, so check them while this is down.
legalQueue.summary: {open} open, {overdue} overdue, {dueSoon} due within 7 days. Clocks count in {zone} time.
legalQueue.banner: {count, plural, one {# legal clock is overdue.} other {# legal clocks are overdue.}}

delivery.stuck: {count, plural, one {# alert email has} other {# alert emails have}} waited over an hour to send. Check the subprocessor-notices worker and its schedule.
delivery.failed: {count, plural, one {# alert email} other {# alert emails}} failed in the last 30 days. Check the email provider and the allowlist.
delivery.noAlert: {count, plural, one {# overdue clock has} other {# overdue clocks have}} had no alert in 26 hours. Check the xos_sweep_legal_queue job and the platform email outbox.
delivery.webhookOff: The on-call channel is not connected, so alerts go by email only.
delivery.noticesStuck: {count, plural, one {# email telling someone a moderation result has} other {# emails telling people a moderation result have}} waited over an hour to send. Check the subprocessor-notices worker and its schedule.
delivery.noticesFailed: {count, plural, one {# email telling someone a moderation result} other {# emails telling people a moderation result}} failed in the last 30 days. Each one is an item here, so tell them another way.
delivery.sweepStale: The hourly sweep has not finished in 2 hours, so no alert is going out. Check the xos_sweep_legal_queue job.
delivery.alertPathFailed: Part of the sweep failed in the last 24 hours, and what it could not send tries again each hour. Check the platform email outbox and the on-call webhook.

add.title: Add an item
add.intro: Add anything that arrives outside XOS. The clock starts when it arrived, not when you enter it.
add.titleHelp: Keep personal data out of this line. Alerts name the reference, never this.
add.receivedHelp: In {zone} time, the zone every clock here counts in. Take it from the message itself.
add.detailsHelp: Only the personal data the work needs. The full message stays in the mailbox.
add.subject: Account it is about
add.subjectHelp: Email of the account the notice names, for the repeat infringer count. Leave empty if there is none.
add.related: Reference of the DMCA notice it answers
add.orgHelp: As the Tenants page shows it. Its deletion is held until this item closes.
add.dueHelp: In {zone} time. The rule cannot compute this one, so check it twice.

facts.subject: Account it is about
facts.reReviewerSame: The person who made the first decision
facts.reReviewerOther: Someone who did not make the first decision

move.title: Move it
move.court: The notifier filed a court action, so the material stays down
move.reReviewHelp: Needed to complete or refuse it. Kept on the record and never sent. Say what you re-read and how you weighed the grounds.
move.told: How you told the person the result
move.toldHelp: Needed to complete or refuse it. Say how and when you sent the result and the reasons, and that you told them who re-reviewed it.
move.outside: This appeal goes to {name}, the outside reviewer. Record their decision once they have made it.

extend.title: Take the extension
extend.reason: Why, as you will tell the person
extend.help: One extension, before the first period ends. The person must be told.

legalQueue.fedNote: This item follows the record that created it, so its state changes when that record does.
legalQueue.customerNote: This clock is the Customer's. Who asked and what they said stay in the Customer's register, and GHXSTSHIP helps when the Customer asks.
legalQueue.earliestNote: Do not restore before {when}. The statute sets the earliest day.

repeat.title: Repeat infringer counts
repeat.intro: Valid, uncontested DMCA notices in each person's busiest 12 months. More than two meets the rule in the Copyright and DMCA Policy. A person decides what happens next.

government.title: Government data requests
government.intro: Requests received per calendar year, for the yearly count the Data Processing Agreement promises. A year with no row is a count of zero.

contacts.title: Backup contacts
contacts.intro: Each Administrator gets every alert by email. A backup contact gets overdue alerts only, with references and dates, never the matter.
contacts.none: No backup contact yet. One full inbox could hide a missed clock.
contacts.name: Name

reviewer.title: Outside reviewer
reviewer.none: None is appointed. An operator re-reviews each moderation appeal afresh and records it. If you appoint one, every appeal goes to them.
reviewer.name: Name

events.Hold Placed: Legal hold placed on the organization

dsar_privacy.label: Data subject request by email
dsar_privacy.source: Privacy Policy 7: confirm in 10 business days and answer in 30 days or a calendar month, whichever is shorter. One extension if you say why inside the first period (GDPR 12(3), California regulations).

dsar_brazil.label: Data subject request from Brazil
dsar_brazil.source: LGPD Article 19 and Privacy Policy 7: confirm at once and give a full statement in 15 days.

dsar_appeal.label: Appeal of a refused data request
dsar_appeal.source: Privacy Policy 7: answer in 45 days, after looking at the appeal afresh and recording the reasons.

account_deletion_email.label: Account deletion by email
account_deletion_email.source: Delete Your Account: finish in 30 days.

privacy_complaint.label: Privacy complaint
privacy_complaint.source: Privacy Policy 7: acknowledge in 30 days and give the outcome without undue delay. The 60 days are our own target.

dmca_notice.label: DMCA notice
dmca_notice.source: 17 U.S.C. 512(c): act expeditiously and tell the uploader promptly. The 2 business days are our own target.

dmca_counter_notice.label: DMCA counter-notice
dmca_counter_notice.source: 17 U.S.C. 512(g): copy to the notifier promptly, then restore between 10 and 14 business days unless the notifier files a court action.

repeat_infringer_review.label: Repeat infringer review
repeat_infringer_review.source: 17 U.S.C. 512(i) and Copyright and DMCA Policy 5. The 5 business days are our own target.

abuse_report.label: Abuse report by email
abuse_report.source: Acceptable Use Policy 6 and Digital Services Act Article 16: decide in a timely way. The 5 business days are our own target.

intimate_image_report.label: Intimate image shared without consent
intimate_image_report.source: Our own target, set to the Take It Down Act's 48 hours from a valid request, kept as if XOS were a covered platform.

child_safety_report.label: Child sexual abuse material
child_safety_report.source: 18 U.S.C. 2258A: report to NCMEC as soon as reasonably possible. The 24 hours are our own target.

listing_report.label: Report of a marketplace listing
listing_report.source: Acceptable Use Policy 6 and Digital Services Act Article 16: decide in a timely way. The 5 business days are our own target.

moderation_appeal.label: Appeal of a moderation decision
moderation_appeal.source: Acceptable Use Policy 7: a fresh, documented re-review, with the person told the result. The 30 days are our own target.

security_report.label: Security report
security_report.source: Responsible Disclosure Policy 2: acknowledge in 3 business days and share a plan in 10.

personal_data_breach.label: Personal data breach
personal_data_breach.source: Data Processing Agreement 9.1: tell Customers in 48 hours. GDPR Article 33: tell regulators in 72 hours where GHXSTSHIP is controller.

accessibility_report.label: Accessibility report
accessibility_report.source: Accessibility Statement 5: respond in 5 business days.

accessibility_review.label: Accessibility review request
accessibility_review.source: Accessibility Statement 6: respond in 10 business days, after looking at the complaint afresh and recording the reasons.

government_request.label: Government data request
government_request.source: Data Processing Agreement 13.6: tell the Customer unless the law forbids it, for which the 2 business days are our own target. The document sets the due date.

omitted_data_return.label: Return of data the export omits
omitted_data_return.source: Data Processing Agreement 10.2 and Terms 11.2: return it in 30 days. Adding it places a legal hold on the organization, so its deletion waits until this item closes.

customer_privacy_help.label: Customer's request for privacy help
customer_privacy_help.source: Data Processing Agreement 8.3: reasonable help. The 14 days are our own target, to fit the Customer's 30-day clock.

other_promise.label: Another written promise
other_promise.source: The document that makes the promise. Enter its date.

dsar_customer_register.label: Request in a Customer's register
dsar_customer_register.source: The Customer's clock (Data Processing Agreement 8.1): 30 days, or 90 extended. XOS only watches it.

abuse_appeal.label: Appeal of a moderation decision, by email
abuse_appeal.source: Acceptable Use Policy 7: a fresh, documented re-review, with the person told the result. The 30 days are our own target.

undelivered_notice.label: Moderation result not delivered
undelivered_notice.source: Acceptable Use Policy 6 and 7: the person is told the result. The 2 business days are our own target.

queue_feed_failure.label: Queue feed failure
queue_feed_failure.source: Our own target: the queue must see every record that starts a clock.

fedTitles.repeat: {count, plural, one {# valid, uncontested DMCA notice} other {# valid, uncontested DMCA notices}}

watched.title: Customer clocks we watch
watched.intro: {count} open. These clocks are each Customer's own. They stay here until the Customer closes them, and never count as work overdue.

legalQueue.undeliveredNote: This person has not been told the result of a moderation decision or appeal. Tell them another way, then complete this item and say how. Who it was for and what it said show below, if we still hold them.
legalQueue.feedFailureNote: One of the queue's automatic feeds is failing, so records of that kind are not reaching this list. Everything else still runs, and this item closes itself when the feed works again. Check the error below and the most recent migration.

ratingDisputes.title: Rating disputes
ratingDisputes.intro: People disputing a rating an organization gave them. The score is not shown, because it cannot decide a dispute. Uphold only on a named ground; the reasons go to the person and the organization.
ratingDisputes.none: No dispute waits for a decision.
ratingDisputes.detailIntro: {person} disputes a rating from {org}, project {project}, given on {when}.
ratingDisputes.notUphold: Do not uphold; the rating stays
ratingDisputes.statement: Reasons sent to the person and the organization
ratingDisputes.statementHelp: Sent as written. Say what you decided and why, without using the score or an opinion as a reason.
ratingDisputes.own: This dispute is your own, or you belong to the organization that gave the rating, so another operator decides it.

billingAlerts.cancel_delayed: Stripe has not accepted a cancel
billingAlerts.active_on_deleted_org: Live subscription on a deleted org
billingAlerts.cancel_missing: Stripe did not know a live subscription
